pos.personaBrief: United dominated possession against Chelsea in the final first half and Scholes/Carrick/Hargreaves recycled the ball to pin teams back, yet they gave up possession to Barcelona and won by sealing space and hitting the front three on the break.

pro.personaBrief: Giggs and Scholes sprayed long diagonals and raking passes to runners in behind, the front three attacked space and counters were quick, while Carrick and Scholes still played vertical passes through midfield.

est.personaBrief: The formation was fluid, with Ronaldo, Rooney and Tevez interchanging, Rooney dropping deep and Giggs moving inside, and Ronaldo cutting in off the wing with Evra overlapping.

lar.personaBrief: Width came from full-backs Evra and Brown, with Ronaldo dribbling inside and Evra overlapping or underlapping, so attacks used the flanks and the wide forwards but not pinned to the touchline.

blo.personaBrief: United defended in a compact 4-4-1-1 or 4-4-2 with Tevez pressing, with pressure on the ball and quick regains, and only dropped deeper in specific games such as the Barcelona semi-final.

mar.personaBrief: No source documents man-marking; defending was a compact collective block with sealed zones, as Ferguson said of Barcelona, so zonal principles dominate and a dedicated marker is not evidenced.

pla.personaBrief: Ferguson adapted by set-up for big ties (Hargreaves deep right, Ronaldo high left, conservative switch with Hargreaves) while keeping an attacking culture, and he picked his side by opponent.

res.personaBrief: United were attacking and entertaining but the goal was trophies; Ferguson set up not to lose away at Barcelona, sealed the areas for a 0-0 and made conservative changes to protect a lead.

sis.personaBrief: A team of stars given freedom of movement within a clear structure, with Ferguson rotating squads, demanding work from everyone (Tevez, Rooney 12km) and tolerating Ronaldo's lower defensive output.

jog.personaBrief: A blend of technique and pace and energy: Ronaldo, Scholes and Carrick on the ball, Rooney and Tevez running over 12km, and Vidic and Ferdinand strong at the back.

bas.personaBrief: A mix of experienced stalwarts (Giggs, Scholes, Van der Sar) and big signings (Anderson, Nani, Hargreaves) with a few academy products; titles were won by seasoned players while young stars like Ronaldo and Rooney were already key.

lid.personaBrief: Ferguson was the boss: he dropped Tevez for not training well and fined Ronaldo after a red card, with authority first and little room for the players to veto his line-up.
